text:
jamie: Heads-up — rerank embeddings route P99 spiked after the kernel swap this morning. Noticed a big tail on short-context requests. Quick stats below, pasted from Grafana snapshot.

jamie: metrics snapshot:
- endpoint: /v1/rerank/embeddings
- QPS: 178 (down from 220)
- p50: 28ms
- p95: 96ms
- p99: 320ms (was ~110ms)
- avg batch size: 6 (mode: 1-4)
- vector dim: 1024
- KV cache hit rate: 87% (was 98%)
- GPU utilization: 62% (some kernels bottlenecked)

ali: Can you paste the profiler output and the kernel selection log? Wondering if the new attention kernel favors long sequences and has higher setup cost for short sequences.

jamie: profiler snippet:
```
[PROFILE] top kernels by total_time
1) matmul_cutlass_fused_fp16 45.1% (calls: 3421)
2) attention_v2_unified 30.3% (calls: 2897)
3) kv_cache_lookup 12.4% (calls: 12458)
4) cuda_memcpy_async 7.8%
5) runtime_dispatch_overhead 4.4%
```
notes: attention_v2_unified has a ~70us setup penalty per call for small seq_len.

ali: OK that aligns. The matmul kernel change increased per-call overhead; for tiny batches the overhead dominates. Also KV hit-rate drop suggests cache keys not matching (maybe change in serialization/quantization of keys during kernel update?).

sophie: Dashboard note — our current per-route KPI panels aggregate embeddings + generation routes. We don't have token-level latency breakdown for rerank endpoints specifically. We should add: dispatch_time, kernel_time (per-kernel), kv_lookup_time, memcpy_time, postproc_time. That will help isolate where p99 is coming from.

miguel: I pulled the KV logs — there was a small change in the eviction policy rollout yesterday (TTL from 30m -> 5m for a test). That explains the hit rate drop. Evictions spiked ~03:10 UTC which aligns with the P99 spike.

jamie: ah yes that TTL change was in the experiment branch. Maybe combine effects: kernel overhead + more cache misses = more work per request -> tail.

ali: Proposed short-term mitigations:
- revert TTL experiment for rerank tenant pool (restore 30m)
- add kernel selection rule: if seq_len <= 128 and avg_batch_size <= 8, prefer matmul_small_batch kernel (lower setup latency)
- tuning: set dynamic_batching.max_delay_ms = 8 for rerank route, disable continuous batching for requests flagged low-latency

ali: config snippet (for runtime routing):
```
{"routes": [{"path": "/v1/rerank/embeddings", "batching": {"max_batch": 64, "max_delay_ms": 8, "prefer_small_batch_kernel": true}, "kv": {"ttl_override_sec": 1800}}]}
```

perf-bot: Automated check:
- baseline (pre-kernel switch): p99=110ms, QPS=220, KV_hit=98%
- current: p99=320ms, QPS=178, KV_hit=87%
- regression detected: p99 +190ms (173% increase), QPS -19%

sophie: I'll add the token-level panels and split per-route histograms. Also will add a per-kernel flamechart widget and surface kernel versions in the route table.

miguel: I'll roll back the TTL change for rerank pools and re-run the nightly cache-warm job. I'll also add an alert when KV_hit_rate drops below 95% for any rerank route.

jamie: Can someone own the kernel selection fallback? ali?

ali: I'll implement the selection rule and add a canary: routes with `prefer_small_batch_kernel` will use the small kernel for 25% of traffic first. I'll push a runtime flag and a metric `kernel_selection_fallback` to track usage.

sophie: Timeline proposals:
- today EOD: rollback TTL and enable cache-warm (miguel)
- tomorrow morning: deploy dashboard panels (sophie)
- tomorrow afternoon: kernel selection change (ali) with 25% canary
- Friday: analyze p99 and QPS, A/B traffic if stable :eyes:

jamie: Thanks. Can we also record a regression test in the perf-suite: synthetic rerank workload (seq_len=64, dim=1024, batch distribution [1..8]) so we catch this in changelists?

ali: Good call — will add a perf test and gate it on p99 <= 130ms for that workload.

jamie: Awesome. TL;DR actions: rollback KV TTL for rerank, add dashboard panels (token-level + per-kernel), implement kernel fallback rule and canary, add perf test. Assign owners above. :thumbsup:

sophie: I'll update the runbook to include KV hit alerts and dashboard links once panels are live.

miguel: Rolling the TTL rollback now, will post status when done.

perf-bot: rollback event detected for experiment/kv-ttl -> rerank-pool by miguel at 1768254420

miguel: rollback complete. cache-warm kicked. KV_hit_rate back to 97% in the warm window.

jamie: Great work team. We'll keep monitoring p99 and QPS — set 24h watch and sync after the kernel canary. :rocket:
